correctness.rationale: For an omitted set X, a selected vertex opposite A misses at most one vertex of A, hence cannot uniquely witness any of three omitted A vertices: omitted counts alpha,beta<=2. When alpha=2 the two omitted A indices must be among the t deleted pairs and their opposite partners selected, equivalently I subset [t], I cap J empty; symmetrically for beta=2. For singleton A-omission, a witness exists except b=3,beta=2 and sole selected opposite vertex is its deleted partner; the symmetric a=3 exception is essential and correctly included. The nine possible occupancy types contribute 1,a,b,ab,C(t,2),C(t,2), corrected (2,1)/(1,2) totals and 6C(t,4). This proves polynomial across all a,b,t, with t=0/1 identical; positivity of top coefficients yields piecewise gamma and special (3,3,3) count 15. Minimum vertex degree min(a,b)-1>=2 makes every super dominating set end-super-dominating under the paper's definition. Independent direct open-neighbour brute enumeration across eight profiles (including all t=0..3 for a=b=3, t=4 for 4x4 and t=5 for 5x5) matched every omitted-size coefficient; the proof, not the finite tests, covers unbounded parts.

final_claim: For a,b>=3 and 0<=t<=min(a,b), the biclique K_{a,b} with t disjoint deleted matching edges has omitted-set super-domination enumerator 1+N u+(ab+2C(t,2))u²+C(t,2)[N-4-(t-2)(1_{a=3}+1_{b=3})]u³+6C(t,4)u⁴, N=a+b; exact gamma and minima multiplicities follow, including exceptional (3,3,3), and t=0,1 are polynomial-identical.
